notes: Account summary: large EU-headquartered fintech (payment rails + risk), high data residency and audit needs — evaluating Redwood Private VPC for model hosting.
Primary ask: private VPC deployment where inference endpoints never traverse public internet; need PrivateLink or VPC peering-based connectivity with strict egress control.
Network specifics discussed on 2026-03-03 call: customer prefers AWS PrivateLink to avoid cross-account peering; open to Transit Gateway if PrivateLink not feasible for all regions.
Egress controls: must provide stable, customer-provided IP allowlist (or static egress IPs from Redwood) to allow firewall outbound rules; explicit requirement from InfoSec.

Firewall & routing: customer will only open TLS to pre-approved Redwood IPs; no inbound allowed except on PrivateLink interface endpoints; they run stateful firewalls and will test with Palo Alto next week.

Egress inspection: security team requires egress traffic to pass through customer-managed proxy for DLP logging — ask: can Redwood route egress via customer's NAT/proxy or provide private endpoints for model IO?
TLS / mTLS: prefer mutual TLS for service-to-service calls; Redwood asked whether mTLS termination can be customer-controlled — outcome: Redwood to propose mTLS option or IP-based trust.

Audit logging: retention requirement = 5+ years for request logs and 3+ years for admin audit trails; customer expects structured audit exports to their SIEM (Splunk) via S3 or Kinesis Firehose.
Data residency: production requests and embeddings must remain in EMEA (Ireland/Frankfurt); any temporary metadata for routing must be scoped and logged.

Customer docs requested: network diagram template, sample firewall rules, egress IP list, KMS integration guide, retention/audit export spec — Redwood to deliver by 2026-03-12.
